title: TypeScript function types, overloads, predicates, and call signatures
concepts: Function types describe accepted arguments and return values
Call and construct signatures allow object types to be callable or constructable
Overload signatures expose multiple valid call shapes
Type predicates connect runtime checks to static narrowing
The implementation signature must support every public overload

inventory.title: Function type and object call signatures
Callbacks, contextual typing, and function compatibility

items: Eligible boolean-returning functions can have an inferred type predicate return signature instead of only boolean.
TypeScript 7.0 stable was announced July 8, 2026; TypeScript 7.1 remained beta as of the audit date. No newer function-signature rule was assumed in this lesson.

sourceSnapshot.authority: Official TypeScript Handbook and release notes

accuracyFacts: A function type expression describes one callable signature; a call signature can be a member of a larger object type that also has properties or multiple call signatures.
An explicit this parameter is erased and is a type-only declaration in the first parameter position; JavaScript's runtime receiver behavior remains separate.
Overload signatures are the public call surface; the implementation signature is hidden from callers and must be compatible with every overload implementation path.
A union-typed argument may fail to match any of several overloads unless there is a suitable overload for the union or a single union-parameter signature.
Under strictFunctionTypes, ordinary function parameter positions are checked contravariantly, while method and constructor parameter positions retain a bivariance compatibility exception.
Optional callback parameters mean callers may omit that argument; a callback that merely ignores an argument can usually declare fewer parameters without marking the last parameter optional.
TypeScript 5.5 inferred type predicates only under the documented conditions and two-way semantics; predicate soundness details and runtime guard behavior are covered in t06-021.
